A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same NegBio-VAE research. All 19 pages of v1 and 20 pages of v2, including equations, figures, tables and appendices, support comparison despite substantial experimental and presentation revisions.

before.justification: V1 reports original benchmark experiments, latent classification results, overdispersion diagnostics and ablations in Section 5 and the appendices.

after.justification: V2 reports original reconstruction, generation, few-shot classification and ablation results in Section 5 and the appendices.

M1.justification: The negative-binomial prior/posterior, Monte Carlo and dispersion-sharing KL strategies, Gamma–Poisson sampling, and Gumbel-Softmax and continuous-time relaxations are retained. The Gaussian decoder description moves from Section 4.3 to Section 5.1.2 without changing the procedure.

E1.justification: Fashion-MNIST and CelebA-64 replace Omniglot and SVHN, replacing multilingual handwriting and street-number coverage with clothing and faces. MNIST and CIFAR16×16 remain, and CIFAR gains downstream classification evaluation.

E2.justification: The main quantitative comparisons retain Gaussian, Laplace, categorical and Poisson VAEs. However, v1's architecture comparison and reconstruction figures include these external baselines, whereas the corresponding v2 figures compare only NegBio-VAE variants. NVAE participation is described inconsistently and has no reported result row, so an evaluated NVAE addition is not established.

E3.justification: V2 replaces IS and latent diagnostic metrics with SSIM and KID, and reports FID at both 5,000 and 10,000 samples. Latent-dimension evaluations change from 10/128/256 to 10/50/100. It adds class-balanced 1/5/10/20-shot protocols with logistic regression and kNN, expands the architecture combinations, and extends the beta sweep from 0.2–0.8 to 0–4.

E4.justification: V2 removes the single-batch overdispersion control, high-dimensional dead-neuron analysis, t-SNE comparison and convergence-statistics summary. Architecture ablations expand from varying encoders with a fixed linear decoder to encoder–decoder combinations across four NegBio-VAE variants. Beta, Monte Carlo sample-count and loss-dynamics analyses are revised; the appendix sampling-distribution validation is retained.

E5.justification: V1 specifies five runs for the main comparison and reports ± values throughout Table 1. V2 reports point estimates for MSE, SSIM and FID, with ± values only for KID, and newly specifies ten repetitions for downstream tests. This does not establish a five-to-ten increase for matched experiments. V1's loss-step standard-deviation summary is also removed.

E6.justification: Benchmark values, latent results and ablation curves are substantially revised, with additional few-shot results and removal of diagnostic results. For example, the 10-dimensional MNIST shattering ranking changes from NegBio-VAE 0.795 versus P-VAE 0.770 in v1 Table 3 to 0.862 versus 0.865 in v2 Table 4. V2 also reports MNIST 20-shot logistic-regression accuracy of 0.865 versus P-VAE's 0.838. Changed protocols prevent interpreting the overall numerical revision as a same-setting performance gain.

T1.justification: The negative-binomial definitions, shared-dispersion KL derivation, Gamma–Poisson identity and Taylor expansion in Appendix A are retained. Shortening intermediate algebra does not change the reasoning. Added standard SSIM/KID descriptions concern evaluation metrics rather than new theoretical results.

C1.justification: The central NB-latent contribution and two KL/two sampling strategies remain. V2 explicitly scopes superiority claims to single-layer VAEs and emphasizes reconstruction, generation and downstream utility. V1's contribution summary more specifically emphasizes biological plausibility, active latent spaces and superiority with low-dimensional latents.

C2.justification: V2 qualifies v1's assertion that analytical KL reduces gradient variance, stating that this is not guaranteed. It replaces overdispersion-focused interpretations with reconstruction–generation trade-offs and interprets shattering as robustness to randomized supervision. The Monte Carlo sample-count discussion changes from particular benefits for MC-C to marginal gains and sampling robustness. The existing theoretical-understanding limitation is retained within the conclusion.

D1.justification: V2 adds a code-availability link, preprocessing descriptions for the replacement datasets, and SSIM/KID computation descriptions. It removes v1's Python version, GPU/CPU specifications, latent-feature extraction choices and explicit 64-dimensional FID feature setting. The PDFs do not establish what FID feature dimensionality replaces that setting.

R1.justification: V2 adds citations on neuronal variability, implicit reparameterization, NVAE, Very Deep VAE and the replacement datasets, while removing the Omniglot and SVHN references. It discusses the restriction to single-layer comparisons. The main positioning as an extension of Poisson VAE, distinct from negative-binomial observation models, remains.

P1.justification: The abstract and introduction are extensively rewritten, and the experimental narrative is reorganized into reconstruction, generation, fragmentation prediction, few-shot learning and ablation subsections. Implementation material moves, limitations merge into the conclusion, appendices are reorganized, and author information changes.

P2.justification: The document changes from single-column to two-column formatting. V2 adds a method-overview diagram and generation grids, reorganizes and colors tables, replaces reconstruction comparisons with variant-specific displays, and redraws ablation and loss plots. V1's t-SNE and diagnostic displays disappear; these are substantial visual changes beyond renumbering.

improvement.justification: New few-shot evidence, SSIM/KID evaluation, a method diagram and code-access information improve coverage and documentation. However, v2 removes overdispersion/dead-neuron controls and most main-table uncertainty reporting, while omitting FID feature settings. Reporting consistency also suffers: NVAE participation is contradictory, and Appendix E.1 claims the highest shattering scores although Table 4 gives P-VAE 0.865 versus NegBio-VAE 0.862 at dimension 10. These substantive benefits and losses prevent a reliable net quality judgment.
